title: CPR (Adult)
steps: Check responsiveness and verify normal breathing.
Call emergency services immediately or direct someone nearby to call.
Place heel of one hand in the center of the chest, interlock the second hand on top.
Compress chest hard and fast at 100-120 beats per minute, at least 2 inches deep.
Allow full chest recoil between compressions. Continue until emergency personnel take over or an AED arrives.
do: Push hard and fast in center of chest
Send someone for an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) immediately
Switch rescuers every 2 minutes if tired to maintain depth
dont: Do not delay starting compressions to check pulse
Do not lean on the chest between compressions
Do not stop compressions for longer than 10 seconds
callEmergencyWhen: Immediately if the person is unresponsive and not breathing or only gasping.

title: Choking
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' and encourage coughing if they can make sounds.
If unable to speak, cough, or breathe, stand behind them and lean them forward.
Deliver 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
Give 5 quick abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) just above the navel.
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object clears or person becomes unresponsive.
do: Encourage forceful coughing if they can cough or breathe
Support the chest with one hand while delivering back blows
Start CPR if the person loses consciousness
dont: Do not perform abdominal thrusts on infants (use back slaps and chest thrusts)
Do not blindly sweep the mouth with fingers
Do not give them water while choking
callEmergencyWhen: Call immediately if the airway cannot be cleared or the person loses consciousness.

title: Severe Bleeding
steps: Apply direct, continuous firm pressure over the wound using a clean cloth or sterile dressing.
Maintain pressure without lifting the cloth to check the wound.
If blood soaks through, add another cloth on top; do not remove original dressing.
Help the person lie down quietly to reduce shock.
Secure the dressing firmly with a bandage once bleeding slows.
do: Maintain firm direct pressure continuously
Keep the person calm, still, and warm
Wear protective gloves if available
dont: Do not remove embedded objects from a deep wound
Do not remove saturated dressings
Do not apply a makeshift tourniquet unless trained and bleeding is uncontrolled life threat
callEmergencyWhen: Call immediately if blood is spurting, will not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure, or person shows signs of shock.

title: Burns
steps: Cool the burn immediately under cool running tap water for at least 10 to 20 minutes.
Remove jewelry, watches, or constricting items near the burn before swelling begins.
Cover loosely with sterile, non-adherent dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Protect the person from becoming chilled while cooling large burns.
do: Use cool running water (not ice-cold)
Keep blistered skin intact to prevent infection
Keep the burn clean and loosely covered
dont: Do not apply ice, ice water, butter, oil, or toothpaste to burns
Do not pop or break any blisters
Do not peel off clothing stuck to the burnt skin
callEmergencyWhen: Call immediately for burns larger than the person's palm, electrical/chemical burns, or burns to the face, hands, joints, or airway.

title: Fractures & Sprains
steps: Immobilize the injured limb in the position found; do not try to realign it.
Apply cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes to reduce swelling.
Support the injury using padding, splints, or slings if movement is necessary.
Elevate the injured limb above heart level only if it does not cause pain.
do: Keep the injured area completely still and supported
Apply ice wrapped in a towel, never directly onto bare skin
Check circulation (warmth, feeling) below the injury regularly
dont: Do not attempt to push exposed bone back into the wound
Do not try to straighten or force an injured limb
Do not allow the person to walk on an injured leg or foot
callEmergencyWhen: Call immediately if bone is visible, limb is cold or blue, joint is completely deformed, or severe bleeding is present.

title: Fainting
steps: Help the person lie flat on their back on the floor.
Elevate their legs about 12 inches (30 cm) if there are no spinal or leg injuries.
Loosen tight collars, belts, or restrictive clothing around the neck and chest.
Ensure plenty of fresh air and check breathing.
Keep them lying down for at least 10-15 minutes after regaining consciousness.
do: Keep them lying flat until fully recovered
Roll them into recovery position if they vomit or feel nauseated
Check for normal breathing and responsiveness
dont: Do not let them stand up quickly after regaining consciousness
Do not slap, shake, or splash cold water on their face
Do not give food or drink while they are semi-conscious
callEmergencyWhen: Call emergency if they remain unconscious for more than 1 minute, hit their head during the fall, or complain of chest pain or shortness of breath.

title: Seizure
steps: Ease the person safely to the floor and clear hard or sharp objects away.
Place a soft, flat cushion or folded clothing under their head.
Loosen tight clothing around their neck.
Note the time the seizure began to monitor its duration.
Once jerking stops, gently roll them onto their side into the recovery position.
do: Time the seizure accurately
Protect head and body from surrounding hazards
Stay calm and reassure them as they wake up
dont: Do not restrain or hold the person down
Do not put anything inside the person's mouth (they will not swallow their tongue)
Do not give fluids or pills until fully alert
callEmergencyWhen: Call immediately if the seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes, repeats without regaining consciousness, occurs in water, or if the person is pregnant or injured.

title: Snake Bite
steps: Move safely away from the snake to avoid further strikes.
Keep the person calm, completely still, and lying down to slow venom spread.
Remove tight jewelry and restrictive clothing from the bitten limb before swelling starts.
Immobilize the affected limb with a splint at or slightly below heart level.
Call emergency services or transport to the nearest hospital immediately.
do: Keep the patient as still and quiet as possible
Remember the snake's color and pattern from a safe distance if possible
Apply a clean, dry dressing over the bite wound
dont: Do not cut the bite wound or attempt to suck out venom
Do not apply a tight tourniquet or ice to the bite
Do not try to capture or kill the snake
callEmergencyWhen: Call emergency services immediately for all suspected venomous snake bites.

title: Heart Attack Signs
steps: Recognize warning signs: chest pain, pressure, squeezing, or pain spreading to arm, neck, jaw, or back.
Call emergency services immediately; do not delay.
Help the person sit down in a comfortable position, typically half-sitting with knees bent and back supported.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and waist to ease breathing.
Stay with the person, monitor breathing, and be prepared to start CPR if they become unresponsive.
do: Call emergency services at the first sign of chest discomfort
Keep the person calm and resting comfortably
Locate the nearest AED if in a public area
dont: Do not let the person walk around or exert themselves
Do not wait to see if symptoms go away on their own
Do not drive them yourself if an ambulance is available
callEmergencyWhen: Call emergency immediately at the first suspicion of heart attack symptoms.

title: Stroke Signs (FAST)
steps: Check Face: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
Check Arms: Ask the person to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
Check Speech: Ask the person to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
Time: If any of these signs are present, call emergency services immediately.
Keep the person lying flat with head slightly elevated, and monitor breathing until help arrives.
do: Note the exact time symptoms first appeared
Keep the patient calm and comfortable
Turn on their side if they vomit or are drooling
dont: Do not give them anything to eat or drink (choking risk)
Do not give any medication without medical instructions
Do not let them go to sleep or wait to see if symptoms improve
callEmergencyWhen: Call emergency services immediately upon seeing any one of the FAST warning signs.
